Definition: to dock off, i.e. curtail (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative); especially to harvest (grass or grain)
BiblicalUsage: To reap is the word for the harvest and its law: when thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it, it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow; they of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley when the ark came back. Hosea says, sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap in mercy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the reaping carries the law of gleaning with it, because the harvest is never only for the harvester. What moves me is that the forgotten sheaf belongs to the stranger, and the sowing in righteousness reaps in mercy, so the field is where justice and grace meet.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
